component: molecules-and-bonding / starterMolecules / Sodium chloride (NaCl) — rendered as its real rock-salt ionic lattice rather than a discrete molecule, since NaCl has no discrete molecular form.
sourceDescription: NaCl is an ionic solid (no discrete 'molecule'), so it has no RCSB PDB Chemical Component Dictionary ligand entry as a compound — only its constituent ions (NA, CL) exist individually in the CCD. Geometry instead uses the standard rock-salt crystal structure: cubic lattice constant a = 5.64 Angstrom (well-established public-domain crystallographic constant), Na+ and Cl- alternating on a simple-cubic grid of spacing a/2 by (i+j+k) parity, which reproduces the correct two-interpenetrating-FCC rock-salt structure. A 3x3x3 grid (one conventional unit cell plus neighbors) is rendered with thin rods along nearest-neighbor axes to make the lattice legible.
